angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 514,818 km at 3.22 pc = 2.14 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 310.5773 +/- 0.1355 mas (same row, RUWE 2.72): 3.22 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 0.74 +/- 0.01 solar radii from Baines & Armstrong (2012), ApJ 744, 138, section 3: the Navy Optical Interferometer limb-darkened angular diameter 2.153 ± 0.028 mas at the parallax of Benedict et al. (2006) (https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.0447): 514,818 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.82 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Thompson et al. (2025), AJ 170, 301, the stellar mass their orbit fit of ε Eridani b adopts, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive default parameter set (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..301T/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5039 +/- 126 K from Baines & Armstrong (2012), ApJ 744, 138, section 3: from the interferometric angular diameter and the bolometric flux (https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.0447). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Baines & Armstrong (2012), ApJ 744, 138, section 3: from the interferometric angular diameter and the bolometric flux (https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.0447)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/eps-eridani.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.613, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of eps Eri (pscomppars): spectral type K2 V, from Llop-Sayson et al. 2021 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162..181L/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of eps Eri (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.13 dex, from Benedict et al. 2006 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2006AJ....132.2206B/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of eps Eri (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.41928, from Gaia DR2 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018A&A...616A...1G/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of eps Eri (pscomppars): age 0.6 Gyr, from Llop-Sayson et al. 2021 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162..181L/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of eps Eri (pscomppars): rotation period 11.1 d, from Thompson et al. 2025 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..301T/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of eps Eri (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 2.4 km/s, from Valenti & Fischer 2005 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2005ApJS..159..141V/abstract)
spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (0.74 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.712. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (HST/STIS Next Generation Spectral Library v2 (Heap & Lindler; MAST high-level science product), HD 22049) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
